ACCEPTNo required correction to the new exact completion theorem or its implementation. The supplied argument establishes, for every  $K\ge l\ge1$ , every actual rematching of the two fixed footprints, and every nonnegative real weighting,
$$\boxed{\min_{N\ \mathrm{full}} f(N)=\min(\rho_1,\rho_2)=\Lambda.}$$
The construction works when the weighted optimum pays the large/left core and assigns the white hole  $z$  to the right core.I reviewed the attached source bundle identified as 1aae8d611cd9aa7f2da68b3761f7c37eef8548a3, starting with    SHARED_SOURCE_EXACT_WEIGHTED_REMATCHING.md. I also executed the requested checker with assertions enabled and verified structural and byte-for-byte equality of its regenerated JSON with the supplied output. The proof review and execution findings are distinguished below.1. The whole outer-region deletion lemma is validThe crucial strengthening in §3 holds for the entire region
$$R=Q\setminus\{h_1,h_2,z\},$$
and for every white  $t\in R$ .Partition and near-perfect matchingThe stated decomposition
$$R=(L_1\setminus\{z\})\;\dot\cup\;L_2\;\dot\cup\;U\;\dot\cup\;D$$
is correct. The two completion blocks occupy disjoint column ranges; the remaining top-right and bottom-left rectangles are exactly  $U,D$ .The initial matching  $A$  is valid: $L_1$  has  $8K+3$  vertices. Deleting  $z$ , at index  $4K$ , leaves segments of lengths  $4K$  and  $4K+2$ . $L_2$  has  $8l+3$  vertices. Deleting its first white vertex  $t_0$  leaves an even path. $U,D$  have even widths and are matched horizontally.These pieces therefore cover precisely  $R\setminus\{t_0\}$ . Every black vertex of  $R$  is matched.Alternating reachabilityThe orientation and reachability argument are correct.First, the ordered  $L_2$  path reaches every white vertex of  $L_2$ : from each even index, a non- $A$  edge reaches the next black vertex, and its  $A$ -edge reaches the next white vertex. The two rectangle entrances also have the required parity and matching orientation:From  $t_0=(4K,W-1)$ , the upward edge enters black  $(4K-1,W-1)\in U$ .From the last white vertex  $(H-1,n_1)\in L_2$ , the leftward edge enters black  $(H-1,n_1-1)\in D$ .In each case, the next  $A$ -edge reaches a white vertex inside the rectangle.The strong-connectivity claim for horizontally matched rectangles is sound. Represent each horizontal matching pair by its white vertex, with a directed transition consisting of a nonmatching white-to-black step followed by the black vertex’s matching edge. Vertically adjacent pairs have transitions in both directions. Between horizontally adjacent pairs, the available direction reverses in an adjacent row. Vertical movement to that row, horizontal movement, and vertical movement back supply the missing direction. Thus every white vertex in either rectangle is reachable. Both rectangles have at least four rows, so the adjacent-row argument has no exceptional minimal case.Finally, the two stated entrances cover all remaining white vertices of  $L_1$ :White  $L_1$  targetReachable white starting vertexIntermediate black vertex $(r,n_1-1)$ , even  $0\le r\le4K-2$  $(r+1,n_1)\in U$  $(r+1,n_1-1)$  $(n_1-1,c)$ , even  $0\le c\le4K$  $(n_1,c+1)\in D$  $(n_1-1,c+1)$ Each intermediate black vertex is matched by  $A$  to the indicated target. The endpoint cases, including  $c=4K$ , are valid.A simple directed path from  $t_0$  to  $t$  therefore alternates correctly. Flipping it matches  $t_0$ , exposes  $t$ , and preserves every other incidence. When  $t=t_0$ , no flip is needed.This proves a perfect matching of all of  $R\setminus\{t\}$ . It resolves the global boundary competition, including entrances above and to the left of the second core; no unsupported assumption that an individually feasible relay extends to a full matching remains.2. Relay existence holds for either core under arbitrary  $M$ The tagged-union argument in §2 does not depend on the canonical actual matching.For any permitted boundary vertex  $c$ , combine a perfect matching of  $S\setminus\{c\}$  with the edge from  $c$  to its exterior white pad  $a$ . This auxiliary matching covers  $S\cup\{a\}$ . Its tagged union with an arbitrary perfect matching of  $S\setminus\{h\}$  has exactly two degree-one vertices,  $h,a$ ; hence they are endpoints of one alternating path. Coincident actual and auxiliary edges are legitimate doubled components and do not invalidate this argument.All three explicit deletions work:Bottom-right corner: vertically match the first  $4k$  rows and horizontally match the remaining even bottom-row interval.Top-left corner: vertically match the last  $4k$  rows and horizontally match the remaining even top-row interval.Bottom midpoint: vertically match the first  $4k$  rows and horizontally match the two remaining intervals, each of length  $2k$ .The shared  $z$  is adjacent to the required corner of each square. Consequently either core can receive the HH relay.The bottom-midpoint white pads are
$$(4K+1,2K),\qquad
(H-1,\,4K+2+2l).$$
Both are on the board, outside  $P$ , white, and different from  $z$ , so both belong to  $T$ . Thus both TH distances are finite for every admissible rematching.For nonnegative real weights, a minimum exists among the finitely many simple candidate paths. Zero weights cause no mathematical difficulty.3. The lower bound and simultaneous full completion agreeLower bound over every full  $N$ Every terminal path begins and ends with auxiliary edges, has odd length, and has opposite-colour endpoints. The two black centres therefore belong to different terminal paths.Only  $z$  is a white hole, so at most one centre can have an HH path. At least one centre has a TH path. Such a path cannot contain another  $Q$  vertex internally, and no grid edge joins  $P_1$  to  $P_2$ . Its internal vertices consequently remain in its own core, and its expense is at least the corresponding  $\rho_i$ . Nonnegativity of all other TH expenses gives
$$f(N)\ge\min(\rho_1,\rho_2).$$
Attainment and resource compatibilityChoose a minimizing TH relay in core  $j$ , with white endpoint  $t$ , and an HH relay from  $z$  to the other centre.Their internal vertices lie in disjoint footprints, and their white endpoints  $t,z$  are distinct. Each relay consumes complete actual  $M$ -pairs. Therefore their auxiliary edges, together with auxiliary copies of every unused actual edge, cover exactly
$$P\cup\{h_1,h_2,z,t\}$$
without collisions.The uncovered set is exactly  $R\setminus\{t\}$ , to which the outer deletion lemma applies. Every added direct edge has a white endpoint in  $T$  and a black endpoint in  $H$ , so it is a zero-expense direct TH component. The HH relay contributes no TH expense, regardless of the weights on its actual edges. Unused actual edges form free tagged doubles.The result is a full  $N$  with expense exactly  $\rho_j$ . This argument is symmetric in the paid-core choice; it includes paying the large/left core and using  $z$  for the right.Feasibility also survives rematching:  $T$  is monochromatic, each selected vertex has at most one neighbour in  $P$ , and the only white exterior vertex adjacent to both cores is the excluded vertex  $z$ . Moreover,
$$|T|=|V|/2-|M|-1,
\qquad J=|V|/2-1.$$
Capacity-one HH budgetEvery black vertex in  $R$  has a direct selected white neighbour, witnessed by  $A$ . Its shortest T-source expense is therefore zero. Only the two centres can have positive terminal lower weights, namely  $\rho_1,\rho_2$ .The one white HH source reaches both centres but can discount only one. Hence
$$\Lambda
=\rho_1+\rho_2-\max(\rho_1,\rho_2)
=\min(\rho_1,\rho_2).$$
This remains correct when one or both distances are zero. The budget never spends  $z$  twice.4. Implementation, predecessors, and complexityThe implementation in   shared_source_exact_completion.py agrees with the proof.The reverse shortest-path graph is correctly confined to one footprint, its centre, and admissible white targets. Black-to-white non- $M$  steps have cost zero; white-to-black actual steps have their prescribed weight. Reconstruction produces the terminal-to-centre path, with actual edges at the correct alternating positions.The lexicographic label  $(\text{expense},\text{hops})$  handles zero weights correctly: every arc adds a strictly positive lexicographic increment, either  $(0,1)$  or  $(w,1)$ . Together with strict improvement and stale-entry rejection, this prevents predecessor cycles. The implementation uses exact integers without a floating conversion or finite infinity sentinel.The outer BFS similarly uses first-visit predecessors, producing a simple alternating exchange path. Final decomposition checks require a full auxiliary matching and correctly preserve the distinction between the actual and auxiliary copies of a doubled edge.The complexity claim is justified: bounded grid degree gives  $O(v)$  arcs; three Dijkstra searches take  $O(v\log v)$  arithmetic operations, and construction, outer BFS, reconstruction, and the linear tagged decomposition take  $O(v)$  additional work. Storage is  $O(v)$  vertex, edge, and numeric records. This is the stated arithmetic model; arbitrary-precision integer bit costs still depend on weight length.5.
